issues.title: Test file separated from component
issues.description: The rule requires that for every React component file component.tsx, the test file component.test.tsx exists in the same directory. However, the test file schema-form-input-array-list.test.tsx was placed in a __tests__ subdirectory instead of being co-located with schema-form-input-array-list.tsx.
issues.rule_name: React Component Test Files Must Be Co-Located

issues.title: Drag-and-drop reordering swaps source and target indices
issues.description: The handleDragEnd function passes arguments to moveItem in the wrong order - it calls moveItem(newIndex, oldIndex) instead of moveItem(oldIndex, newIndex). This causes drag-and-drop operations to place items in the opposite position from where they're dropped. For example, dragging an item from index 2 to index 0 will incorrectly move the item at index 0 to index 2 instead, creating confusing and incorrect reordering behavior for users.

issues.title: Prefix items incorrectly included in sortable context
issues.description: The sortableKeys array is constructed from all localKeyedValues instead of excluding prefix items. The code removed the .slice(prefixItemsCount) operation, meaning prefix items (which should have fixed positions and not be draggable) are now included in the SortableContext. This allows prefix items to be moved via drag-and-drop, violating the constraint that prefix items must remain in their fixed positions and breaking the schema's structural requirements.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
// Get the keys of items that can be dragged (non-prefix items)
const sortableKeys = localKeyedValues.map((item) => item.key);

issues.title: Unused local variable `prefixItemsCount` added
issues.description: `prefixItemsCount` is introduced but never referenced anywhere in the component. This leaves unused code in the codebase, violating the rule requiring unused items to be removed.
issues.rule_name: Unused Imports Must Be Automatically Removed

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #20223 - Add drag-and-drop reordering for schema form arrays

structured_output.summary:
This PR replaces the reorder-by-menu-only UX for schema form arrays with drag-and-drop built on @dnd-kit. A `DndContext` and `SortableContext` wrap the list in `schema-form-input-array-list.tsx`, and each row in `schema-form-input-array-item.tsx` becomes a `useSortable` element with a `GripVertical` handle. Prefix items (tuples) render without a handle and are marked `disabled`. The existing Move up/Move down menu items are kept, and four snapshot tests cover handle visibility and prefix rendering.

The core drag path has a real bug. `handleDragEnd` calls `moveItem(newIndex, oldIndex)`, but `moveItem(from, to)` takes its arguments in the opposite order, so any drag that moves an item more than one slot moves the wrong item. Separately, drops are not clamped away from prefix indices, so a regular item can be dropped into a tuple slot and the value-to-schema mapping breaks. The tests only check rendered DOM and never exercise `handleDragEnd`, which is why neither problem is caught. The PR description also claims behavioral tests for move up/down and for prefix immovability, and the diff contains neither.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The drag-and-drop path, which is the headline feature, reorders the wrong item for any non-adjacent move because of the reversed `moveItem` arguments. Drops are also not blocked from landing on prefix (tuple) slots, which can reassign values to schemas they don't match. Both are must-fix before merge. The test additions are snapshot-only and do not cover the reorder logic, so they give false confidence about the feature.

architecture.overview:
Schema forms render arrays through `SchemaFormInputArray`, which delegates non-enum arrays to `SchemaFormInputArrayList`. That component owns a local keyed copy of the array values (`localKeyedValues`, with uuid keys) and exposes add, delete, and move operations that call `onValuesChange` to push the new array to the parent form. Before this PR, reordering was only possible through the per-item dropdown menu's Move up and Move down actions.

This PR adds a dnd-kit layer on top of that model. `SchemaFormInputArrayList` wraps its rows in a `DndContext` with pointer and keyboard sensors and a `SortableContext` keyed by the same uuids. Each `SchemaFormInputArrayItem` registers itself with `useSortable` and renders a drag handle only when `canMove` is true, which is false for prefix (tuple) indices. A drag end is translated into a local `moveItem` call, which shares the same code path as the menu actions.
steps: Entry point: `SchemaFormInputArray` (`schema-form-input-array.tsx`) hands non-enum arrays to `SchemaFormInputArrayList`, which keeps the keyed local state and `moveItem`/`addItem`/`deleteItem` helpers.

The list now wraps its rows in `DndContext` (PointerSensor and KeyboardSensor with `sortableKeyboardCoordinates`) and `SortableContext` over all item keys. Prefix items are still included in the sortable key list.

Each row, `SchemaFormInputArrayItem`, calls `useSortable({ id: itemKey, disabled: !canMove })`, attaches the node ref and transform style, and places the grip button with dnd-kit `attributes` and `listeners` on the first grid column. Prefix rows get an empty `w-5` spacer instead.
On drop, `handleDragEnd` looks up the old and new indices by key and calls `moveItem`. This is the step where the argument order is reversed and where prefix indices are not guarded.
The menu path (Move up / Move down) is unchanged and still calls `moveItem(index, index ± 1)` with the correct order, so the two entry points now disagree on argument convention.

findings.title: Drag-and-drop reorders the wrong item (arguments to moveItem are reversed)
findings.body:
`handleDragEnd` calls `moveItem(newIndex, oldIndex)`, but `moveItem` is defined as `moveItem(from, to)`. The arguments are swapped, so any drag that moves an item by two or more slots pulls the wrong element out of the list.

For example, take `[A, B, C, D]` and drag `A` (old 0) onto `C` (new 2). The code runs `moveItem(2, 0)`, which removes `C` and inserts it at the front, giving `[C, A, B, D]`. The expected result is `[B, C, A, D]`. Adjacent swaps look correct only by coincidence, which is why this could pass casual testing.

The menu's Move up and Move down actions call `moveItem(index, index ± 1)` in the correct order, so the two paths now use different argument conventions.

::diff{file="ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form-input-array-list.tsx" lines="130-145"}

::callout{type="warning"}
No test exercises `handleDragEnd` or `moveItem` with a non-adjacent move, so this passes the suite.

Fix: call `moveItem(oldIndex, newIndex)`, so the source is removed first and the target index is used as the insertion point. Then add a test that drags a non-adjacent item and asserts the resulting value order.
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form-input-array-list.tsx`, `handleDragEnd` (around lines 130-145) calls `moveItem(newIndex, oldIndex)`, but `moveItem(from, to)` (around line 117) expects the source index first. Swap the arguments so it calls `moveItem(oldIndex, newIndex)`. Keep the existing `oldIndex !== -1 && newIndex !== -1` guard. Add a unit test that renders an array of at least four string items, simulates a drag-end from index 0 to index 2 (or calls the DnD handler directly), and asserts the resulting `onValuesChange` payload is `[B, C, A, D]`. Keep the menu Move up/down path unchanged.

findings.title: Drag-and-drop can drop regular items into prefix (tuple) slots
findings.body:
Prefix items are only excluded from dragging through `disabled: !canMove` on the dragged element. Nothing in `handleDragEnd` checks whether `newIndex` is a prefix index, and every key, including prefix keys, is passed into `SortableContext`. A regular item dropped over a prefix row therefore reaches `moveItem` and takes that tuple position.

The schema is chosen by position (`getPropertyForIndex`). After such a drop, a string in position 0 is validated and rendered against the boolean tuple schema, and the prefix row shifts to a regular position. That breaks the tuple contract that the PR description says must hold.

I could not check this against the installed dnd-kit, because `node_modules` is not present in this checkout. Whether a disabled sortable can be reported as `over` depends on dnd-kit internals. The missing guard is a problem either way, because nothing else prevents the move.

::diff{file="ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form-input-array-list.tsx" lines="133-143"}

::callout{type="warning"}
A prefix row only keeps its position if drops that would land on prefix indices are rejected. The existing `getCanMoveForIndex` helper already encodes this rule and should be reused.

Fix: when the target index is a prefix index, return without calling `moveItem`. Alternatively, exclude prefix keys from `sortableKeys` so they are not part of the sortable set at all.
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form-input-array-list.tsx`, `handleDragEnd` (around lines 130-145) moves items without checking whether the target is a prefix (tuple) index. Add a guard that rejects the move when `newIndex` is a prefix index, using the existing `getCanMoveForIndex(newIndex)` helper (around lines 93-98) or an equivalent check. Also consider excluding prefix keys from `sortableKeys` (around line 148) so they are not sortable targets. Add a test that a regular item dropped on the prefix position leaves the prefix item and the value order unchanged.

findings.title: PR description claims behavioral tests that do not exist in the diff
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form.snapshot.test.tsx`, the `describe("array")` block (around lines 489-566) only has snapshot tests. Add behavioral tests in a non-snapshot test file alongside `schema-form.test.tsx` that cover: (1) clicking Move up and Move down in the item menu reorders values and calls `onValuesChange` with the correct order; (2) a drag-end between non-adjacent items reorders correctly (after the moveItem argument fix); (3) prefix items have no drag handle and cannot be moved via the menu or drag. Assert on the resulting values, not on internal calls. Follow the spy/assertion style used in `schema-form.test.tsx`.

findings.title: Snapshots depend on a global dnd-kit ID counter and test order
findings.fixPrompt: The new array snapshots in `ui-v2/src/components/schemas/__snapshots__/schema-form.snapshot.test.tsx.snap` contain dnd-kit generated IDs (`DndDescribedBy-N`, `DndLiveRegion-N`) that depend on a module-level counter and therefore on test order. Make these tests stable: either mock or reset the dnd-kit id generation, or assert on the drag-handle attributes (`aria-roledescription`, `aria-label`, `tabindex`) with targeted expectations instead of full-DOM snapshots. Then regenerate only the affected snapshots and confirm each test passes when run alone with `-t`.

findings.title: Drag handle removes its focus outline without a replacement
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form-input-array-item.tsx`, the drag handle `<button>` (around lines 84-90) uses `focus:outline-none` with no replacement focus indicator, so keyboard users cannot see which handle is focused. Replace it with `focus-visible:outline-hidden focus-visible:ring-1 focus-visible:ring-ring` (the same focus classes the dropdown trigger uses in the snapshot file), keeping the existing layout classes. Update the affected snapshots after the change.

findings.title: Unused prefixItemsCount variable and misleading sortable key comment
findings.body:
`prefixItemsCount` is computed in `schema-form-input-array-list.tsx` but never read, so it is dead code. The comment above `sortableKeys` says it only contains "non-prefix items", but the code maps over every item, including prefix items. The comment misleads readers about the sortable set, and the prefix exclusion is in fact implemented only through `disabled` on the item. Remove the variable, and either fix the comment or exclude prefix keys from the sortable set (see the prefix finding).

::code{file="ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form-input-array-list.tsx" lines="45-48"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form-input-array-list.tsx`, remove the unused `prefixItemsCount` variable (around lines 45-47). Also fix the comment above `sortableKeys` (around line 147), which says it contains only non-prefix items, but the code includes every key. Make the comment accurate, or change `sortableKeys` to exclude prefix keys as part of the prefix fix.

findings.title: Reorder is wired through dnd-kit while keeping the existing menu fallback
findings.body:
The PR keeps the existing `moveUp` and `moveDown` callbacks and the `canMove`, `first`, and `last` checks, so the accessible menu path continues to work alongside drag. Stable uuid keys are used as sortable IDs, so a row's identity survives reorders and the `key` prop stays stable.

Sensor setup uses `sortableKeyboardCoordinates` for keyboard support, and the dragged item fades to 0.5 opacity. Both are the recommended dnd-kit patterns and give users feedback during a drag.
